notes: ACCESS: this is a NetSuite SuiteCommerce Advanced (SCA) storefront, fully client-side rendered. Two routes were used and cross-checked: (1) curl_cffi via probe.py for the server-side HTML and the SCA Items service - HTTP 200 on every request across chrome131/safari15_5/safari17_2_ios; (2) WebFetch for the RENDERED listing headers, which is the only way to read this theme's own '#### N Products' element. ROBOTS: https://www.scullyandscully.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request (938 bytes). It names Claude explicitly and ALLOWS it - there are three separate named groups 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Allow: /', 'User-agent: Claude-Web / Allow: /' and 'User-agent: Claude-SearchBot / Allow: /', under a comment header '# AI/LLM crawlers - explicitly allowed'. No Claude group carries any Disallow, and there is no Crawl-delay. The generic '*' group is 'Allow: /' with Disallow only on /app/site/query/, /search, /checkout, /my_account, /*?*sort= and /*?*filter=. I requested NONE of those: no /search, no sort or filter query URL, and the API endpoint I used is /api/items?... which matches no Disallow pattern (the disallowed service path is /app/site/query/, a different endpoint). probe.py's 2s per-host gap was honoured. TREE: two independent complete sources that agree. (1) The full mega-menu is present server-side in the homepage HTML - 605 anchors parsed with BeautifulSoup, giving 10 departments: Jewelry, Home Decor, Furniture, Tabletop, Collectibles, Herend, Gift Ideas, Inspiration, New Arrivals and Wedding Registry, each expanded to its second and third level. (2) The XML sitemap (sitemap index -> sitemap_www.scullyandscully.com_1690203290_1.xml, 24,365 URLs) of which 391 are multi-segment category paths. I keyword-swept BOTH sources plus all 24,365 sitemap URLs for bath|shower|toilet|vanity|basin|sink|towel|soap|faucet|tap|wc|sanitary|tub|bidet. There is NO Bathroom, Bath, Bath Accessories or Bathroom Accessories category at any level in either source. The Home Decor department's children are Clocks, Holiday Decor, Home Decor Accessories, Leather Accessories, Luxury Lamps, Mirrors, Office Accessories and Picture Frames - no bath node. WHERE THE BATH PRODUCTS LIVE: the sitemap keyword sweep did surface real bath PDPs (eris-pearl-white-marble-bath-accessories, light-green-onyx-bath-collection, botanica-bath-collection, white-marble-bath-accessories, eris-zafferano-verde-onyx-honed-finish-bath-accessories, bamboo-screen-robins-egg-bathroom-accessories, indigo-garden-bathroom-accessories-blue-and-white, eris-black-zebra-marble-wastebaskettissue-box-cover), so I resolved their categories from the storefront's own API rather than guessing: /api/items?url=<slug>&fieldset=details returns a commercecategory.primarypath, and for the Eris Pearl White Marble Bath Accessories it is More Home Accessories (id 686) -> Home Decor Accessories (id 37) -> Home Decor (id 5). A catalogue-wide query /api/items?q=bath returns total 18, of which only 9 are genuine bath accessories and every one of them resolves into Home Decor Accessories. There is no bathroom listing URL to record. QTY METHOD: the SCA Items service, GET /api/items?limit=1&custitem_is_subitem=false&commercecategoryurl=<category path>, field 'total'. CALIBRATION (carried over from the Furniture pass and re-proven here): the RAW api total is inflated because it counts matrix sub-items; adding custitem_is_subitem=false reproduces the site's own rendered header. I re-demonstrated the inflation this session on four categories - More Home Accessories 108 filtered vs 112 raw, Shop All Home Decor Accessories 1279 vs 1329, Vases & Cachepots 206 vs 230, Umbrella Stands 59 vs 60 - so the filter is mandatory and was applied to every figure above. VERIFICATION: every review figure was checked against the RENDERED '#### N Products' listing header via WebFetch, on FIVE pages spanning 22 to 256 items: Round Mirrors API 27 vs rendered 'Round Mirrors / 27 Products'; Nature Mirrors 22 vs '22 Products'; Rectangular Mirrors 80 vs '#### 80 Products'; More Home Accessories 108 vs '108 Products'; Wastebaskets & Tissue Box Covers 256 vs '256 Products'. Five of five exact matches, and each rendered H1 matched the node requested. DISCRIMINATION: 0, 22, 27, 60, 80, 108, 145, 256, 621, 1932 - no site-wide constant. NO AGGREGATION: the Mirrors children overlap (80+60+27+22 = 189 against a Shop All of 145), which is exactly why rule 26's no-aggregation rule matters here; nothing was summed. CONFIRMED ABSENT: Scully & Scully is a Park Avenue luxury gift, furniture, jewellery and tabletop retailer. It sells NO bathroom fixtures or sanitaryware of any kind - no baths, basins, sinks, toilets, bidets, showers, enclosures, screens, taps, faucets, vanity units, bathroom cabinets or bathroom storage - and it has no Bathroom department, no bath accessories listing and no bathroom or vanity mirror. Its only bathroom-typed products are about nine marble and onyx vanity-accessory sets merchandised inside Home Decor > Home Decor Accessories > More Home Accessories, which is a decor node. Per rules 2, 24 and 29 there is no valid Bathroom leaf, so rows is empty and all eight findings are documented in review. CROSS-FILE DEDUP: lib/dedup.already_extracted() was run on all 11 candidate URLs (the five Mirrors nodes, wastebaskets-tissue-covers, more-home-home-accessories, painted-wooden-deco-trays, leather-travel-organizers, bags-cases and the mirrors parent). ZERO hits. The index holds 32 scullyandscully.com URLs, ALL from Furniture.xlsx and all under /furniture/ (seating, cabinets-bookcases-chests, tables, folding-furniture, desks/office, beds, contemporary, miscellaneous); the earlier Home Decor pass (Final.xlsx) contains no scullyandscully.com URL at all, so the Mirrors and Home Decor Accessories nodes above are NOT dedup hits - they are excluded on classification grounds (they belong to Decor/Wall Decor, which is a different category file's problem) rather than on dedup grounds. Nothing was removed from rows for dedup.

There is no bathroom, vanity, LED, illuminated, backlit, demister, cabinet, shaving or magnifying mirror anywhere in the Mirrors department - I checked the whole department item-by-item and separately queried the catalogue for 'vanity', 'shaving' and 'magnifying' (the only hits are a Burl Wood Vanity Tray, Limoges Vanity Boxes, a lacquered Vanity Tray, an Edwardian Shaving Set, leather grooming kits and sterling magnifying glasses - none a mirror). The bath items in it are the marble/onyx vanity sets - Eris Pearl White Marble Bath Accessories, Eris Zafferano Verde Onyx Honed Finish Bath Accessories, White Marble Bath Accessories, Light Green Onyx Bath Collection, Botanica Bath Collection, Bamboo Screen Robin's Egg Bathroom Accessories, Indigo Garden Bathroom Accessories, Black Zebra Marble Bath Accessories, Eris Light Green Onyx Guest Towel Tray - roughly 9 of 108. Under rules 13/18 those 9 individual products would be Bathroom accessories, but the NODE's primary product type is miscellaneous decorative home accessories and there is no bathroom child beneath it, so no Bathroom leaf can be recorded here without misclassifying ~99 decor items. Recorded so the bath line is not silently skipped.
